headline: Council approves new cycle lane budget
body: The city council voted on Tuesday to approve a budget of 2.4 million for new cycle lanes. The measure passed with a clear majority after a two hour debate.

headline: Report claims tap water turns people into lizards
body: A widely shared post claims that municipal tap water contains a compound that slowly turns residents into lizards. No laboratory has confirmed the claim.

headline: Rail operator announces timetable change
body: The national rail operator said timetables will change from next month, adding two evening services on the northern line.

headline: Study links moon phases to stock market crashes
body: An anonymous blog says that stock market crashes always happen during a full moon, citing a chart with no sources.

headline: Health agency publishes flu season summary
body: The public health agency reported that this season's influenza activity peaked in early February and has declined since.

headline: Celebrity secretly replaced by robot, insiders say
body: Insiders claim that a well known actor was replaced by a robot three years ago and that the public never noticed.

headline: University opens new materials laboratory
body: The university opened a materials laboratory on Monday, supported by a regional research grant.

headline: Scientists confirm chocolate cures all known illnesses
body: A viral article states that a single bar of chocolate each day cures every known illness, attributing the finding to unnamed scientists.

headline: Water utility completes pipe replacement
body: The water utility finished replacing 12 kilometres of pipe in the eastern district, restoring normal pressure.

headline: Government plans to ban all cars next month
body: A post circulating online says the government will ban privately owned cars next month. No official document supports this.

headline: Museum returns loaned artefacts
body: The museum returned a collection of loaned artefacts to its partner institution after the exhibition closed.

headline: Miracle mineral water reverses ageing, clinic claims
body: A private clinic claims its mineral water reverses ageing in two weeks, offering testimonials instead of trial data.

headline: Airport reports record passenger numbers
body: The airport handled a record number of passengers last year, according to figures released on Thursday.

headline: Secret tunnel connects parliament to a casino, blogger says
body: A blogger says an undocumented tunnel links the parliament building to a casino, citing a blurry photograph.

headline: Coastal town rebuilds after storm damage
body: The coastal town completed repairs to its promenade and reopened the seafront to visitors.

headline: Firm sells devices that read minds through wifi
body: An online store sells a headset it says reads thoughts through household wifi signals and predicts dreams.

headline: Library extends weekend opening hours
body: The central library will open two hours earlier on weekends from April, funded by a small grant.

headline: Ancient code proves aliens built the pyramids, site says
body: A website says a newly translated code proves that visitors from another planet built the pyramids.

headline: Regional election turnout rises slightly
body: Turnout in the regional election rose by two points compared with the previous vote, officials said.

headline: Hospital uses magnets instead of anaesthesia, post claims
body: A viral post claims a hospital replaced anaesthesia with magnets. The hospital said the claim is false.

headline: Ferry service resumes after maintenance
body: The ferry service resumed its regular schedule after three weeks of scheduled maintenance.

headline: Bottled air from mountains sold online
body: Sellers offer bottled mountain air said to improve concentration. Buyers report no measurable effect.

headline: Council publishes annual budget summary
body: The council published a summary of its annual budget, including spending on parks and transport.

headline: Hidden microchips found in cereal, warns video
body: A video warns that cereal boxes contain hidden microchips used to track shoppers. Food agencies report no evidence.
